d.d: Belonging to us, excluding the person(s) being addressed (exclusive our).
d.x: Sorry, you're not invited to our party.

d.d: Belonging to us, including the person(s) being addressed (inclusive our).
d.x: We must try to save our marriage for the sake of our children.

d.d: Of, from, or belonging to any entity that the speaker is a part of or identifies with, such as place of employment or education, nation, region, language, etc.
d.x: Our safety record at ABC Widgets is very good.

d.d: A serpent, dragon or worm that eats its own tail, a representation of the continuous cycle of life and death.
Anything of a circular or recursive nature.
Excluding the person(s) being addressed (exclusive ours)
d.x: You can't take that! It's ours!

d.d: Including the person(s) being addressed (inclusive ours).
d.x: We should ask for it back. After all, it is ours.

d.d: That or those belonging to any entity that the speaker is a part of or identifies with, such as place of employment or education, nation, region, language, etc.
d.x: French food is better than ours.

d.d: The reflexive of the royal or editorial we: myself (as used by one who is a monarch, writer or speaker when referring to oneself as we).
d.x: In the present study, we will limit ourself to the simplest of cases.

d.d: The reflexive of the generic we: oneself.
d.x: We should love our neighbor as ourself.

d.d: Reflexive of "we" referring to an individual person being addressed, especially a person in the speaker's care.
d.x: Hello Mrs Miggins. Did we manage to wash ourself this morning?

d.d: Us; the group including the speaker as the object of a verb or preposition when that group also is the subject.
d.x: We should keep this for ourselves.

d.d: Intensifies the subject as the group including the speaker, especially to indicate that no one else satisfies the predicate or needs to be included.

d.x: Come on everyone! Let's get ourselves up and out of bed, please.
